The formula below is used to calculate an estimate for the blood alcohol content (BAC) of males.

$$\text{BAC}_{male}=\dfrac{10N-7.5H}{6.8M}$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours between the first and the last drink, and $M$ is the mass in kilograms.

Stephen weighs 98 kilograms. He consumed 6.5 standard drinks between 6:00 pm and 9:45 pm. He then stopped drinking alcohol.

His BAC reached zero at 1:15am. Calculate the rate at which his body metabolised the alcohol, in terms of BAC per hour. Give your answer correct to four decimal places.

notes: Setter is Maths Bank (label 2023 MathsBank AT4; no school named). Solutions merged from separate marking-guidelines file 849 (pages 1-23). Section I = 15 MCQ (15 marks), Section II Q16-38 = 85 marks, total 100. Tables that are images (Q8, Q13, Q15, Q28, Q29, Q36, Q38) are stored as cropped figures. Paper typos kept as printed: Q18 'how many of then are rejected' (then -> them); Q31(b) says the population will 'return to its initial population of 1000' although the guidelines solve for when it falls below 1000; Q28 says all departures/arrivals are on 'the same Sunday' while the guidelines (correctly) treat Sydney departure as Saturday in Dubai time. Guideline errors: Q29(b) total repaid printed as $317 025.40 but 60 x 5117.09 = $307 025.40 (corrected in solution, see edited_from_original); Q31(a) guideline shows '1.89 x 1000' for 1.8^9 x 1000 (written as 1.8^9); Q3 guideline just says 'Line 2' then gives corrected working; minor wording typos in guidelines (Q9 'the the', Q11 'Therefore be options', Q15 'sam'). Q20 guideline shows two valid minimum spanning trees; Q24(b) guideline graph and Q32(a) completed tree and Q35(a) minimum-cut drawing are cropped as solution figures. Q11 option figures: A=q11_1, B=q11_2, C=q11_3, D=q11_4.
